ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the accompanying figure, four squares with side length 1 form a stair-shaped unit grid structure. Point A is located at the lower-left corner of the leftmost lower square, and point B is located at the upper-right corner of the rightmost upper square; line segment AB passes diagonally through these squares. Reasoning: Establish a coordinate system according to the unit grid, and let A=(0,0). Counting along the grid in the figure, B spans 3 unit side lengths to the right relative to A and 2 unit side lengths upward, so B=(3,2). Using the distance formula, AB = sqrt((3-0)^2 + (2-0)^2) = sqrt(9+4) = sqrt(13).

raw_record.question_text: What is the length of line $AB$ if the side of each of the four squares shown is 1?

method.method_draft: Assign coordinates based on the unit-square grid visible in the image. Read A as the bottom-left corner of the lower-left square. Moving from A to B along the grid, B is 3 unit side-lengths to the right and 2 unit side-lengths up, because the four unit squares form a staircase occupying a 3-by-2 bounding grid. Thus take A=(0,0) and B=(3,2). Apply the distance formula to get AB=sqrt((3-0)^2+(2-0)^2)=sqrt(13).
